summary_paraphrase: A wordless book: Dad brings home a new red umbrella and hangs it up, out of bounds, to keep for a rainy day. One by one the children, Grandma and Mom secretly use it for everything but rain: a den, a paper-plane target, a carrot basket, a sunshade, a walking stick. When the storm finally comes and Dad needs it, the hook is empty; the family finds it upside down in the yard, full of rain, a pool for the household duck.

beats.function: weather turns: the rainy day arrives

characters.name: Dad
characters.desire: to keep the umbrella for rain
characters.change: (inferred) his rule fails; he ends smiling
characters.relation_to_protagonist: owner of the umbrella, sets the rule

characters.name: Grandma
characters.humor_source: bunny slippers; carrots in the umbrella

characters.name: (yellow duck)
characters.relation_to_protagonist: household pet present on every page
characters.humor_source: steals a sock, hides, ends up with the umbrella
characters.change: none; it is the running visual gag and the final reveal

humor_notes: Visual irony throughout: a rain umbrella used for everything but rain, including against the sun; the adults break the rule as much as the children; the duck is a hide-and-seek gag on every page.

repetition.description: the same forbidden object reappears in a new secret use on each spread
repetition.why: a wordless pattern the child can predict and name ('now Grandma has it!')

repetition.description: the empty wall hook (p2 full, p7 and p10 empty) marks the rule and its failure
repetition.why: one recurring prop carries the story's question without words

notes: Wordless: all information is in the picture, so every page-turn effect is visual.
Page 9 is a four-panel time-lapse of the same skyline: a wordless countdown to the rain.
Pages 11-12 split a reveal across the turn: faces staring at the window, then what they saw.
The duck appears on every spread as a find-it companion.

strengths: one object, many uses: a simple pattern a pre-reader can follow alone
the rule is broken by adults too, so no one is singled out
the climax reveal is held across a page turn
weaknesses: wordless: the 'saved for a rainy day' premise is only on the publisher's blurb; a young reader may not infer Dad's intent
pages 3-8 are a list of uses with low stakes until the rain arrives

anti_patterns.note: nothing is at risk while the umbrella is borrowed; tension only comes with the rain

child_appeal_heuristic.rationale: Scores are the analyst's reading of the pages, not observations of children. Participation scored for wordless retelling and finding the duck.

age_suitability.notes: Gentle domestic rule-breaking with no punishment shown; no peril.

metrics.lexicon_note: direct_address and sound_words are lexicon counts: a floor, not a measure. direct_address counts second-person words anywhere, dialogue included — it is not narrator-to-reader address

repetition.end_rhyme_note: heuristic: consecutive lines sharing a final two letters
